lines.text: Lady Beatrice, have you wept all this while?
lines.plainText: Lady Beatrice have you wept all this while

lines.text: Yea, and I will weep a while longer.
lines.plainText: Yea and I will weep a while longer

lines.text: I will not desire that.
lines.plainText: I will not desire that

lines.text: You have no reason; I do it freely.
lines.plainText: You have no reason I do it freely

lines.text: Surely I do believe your fair cousin is wronged.
lines.plainText: Surely I do believe your fair cousin is wronged

lines.text: Ah! how much might the man deserve of me that would right her.
lines.plainText: Ah how much might the man deserve of me that would right her

lines.text: Is there any way to show such friendship?
lines.plainText: Is there any way to show such friendship

lines.text: A very even way, but no such friend.
lines.plainText: A very even way but no such friend

lines.text: May a man do it?
lines.plainText: May a man do it

lines.text: It is a man's office, but not yours.
lines.plainText: It is a man's office but not yours

lines.text: I do love nothing in the world so well as you: is not that strange?
lines.plainText: I do love nothing in the world so well as you is not that strange

lines.text: As strange as the thing I know not. It were as possible for me to say I loved nothing so well as you; but believe me not, and yet I lie not; I confess nothing, nor I deny nothing. I am sorry for my cousin.
lines.plainText: As strange as the thing I know not It were as possible for me to say I loved nothing so well as you but believe me not and yet I lie not I confess nothing nor I deny nothing I am sorry for my cousin

lines.text: By my sword, Beatrice, thou lovest me.
lines.plainText: By my sword Beatrice thou lovest me

lines.text: Do not swear by it, and eat it.
lines.plainText: Do not swear by it and eat it

lines.text: I will swear by it that you love me; and I will make him eat it that says I love not you.
lines.plainText: I will swear by it that you love me and I will make him eat it that says I love not you

lines.text: Will you not eat your word?
lines.plainText: Will you not eat your word

lines.text: With no sauce that can be devised to it. I protest I love thee.
lines.plainText: With no sauce that can be devised to it I protest I love thee

lines.text: Why then, God forgive me!
lines.plainText: Why then God forgive me

lines.text: What offence, sweet Beatrice?
lines.plainText: What offence sweet Beatrice

lines.text: You have stayed me in a happy hour: I was about to protest I loved you.
lines.plainText: You have stayed me in a happy hour I was about to protest I loved you

lines.text: And do it with all thy heart.
lines.plainText: And do it with all thy heart

lines.text: I love you with so much of my heart that none is left to protest.
lines.plainText: I love you with so much of my heart that none is left to protest

lines.text: Come, bid me do anything for thee.
lines.plainText: Come bid me do anything for thee

lines.text: Kill Claudio.
lines.plainText: Kill Claudio

lines.text: Ha! not for the wide world.
lines.plainText: Ha not for the wide world

lines.text: You kill me to deny it. Farewell.
lines.plainText: You kill me to deny it Farewell

lines.text: Tarry, sweet Beatrice.
lines.plainText: Tarry sweet Beatrice

lines.text: I am gone, though I am here: there is no love in you: nay, I pray you, let me go.
lines.plainText: I am gone though I am here there is no love in you nay I pray you let me go

lines.text: Beatrice,—
lines.plainText: Beatrice

lines.text: In faith, I will go.
lines.plainText: In faith I will go

lines.text: We'll be friends first.
lines.plainText: We'll be friends first

lines.text: You dare easier be friends with me than fight with mine enemy.
lines.plainText: You dare easier be friends with me than fight with mine enemy

lines.text: Is Claudio thine enemy?
lines.plainText: Is Claudio thine enemy

lines.text: Is he not approved in the height a villain, that hath slandered, scorned, dishonoured my kinswoman? O! that I were a man. What! bear her in hand until they come to take hands, and then, with public accusation, uncovered slander, unmitigated rancour,—O God, that I were a man! I would eat his heart in the market-place.
lines.plainText: Is he not approved in the height a villain that hath slandered scorned dishonoured my kinswoman O that I were a man What bear her in hand until they come to take hands and then with public accusation uncovered slander unmitigated rancourO God that I were a man I would eat his heart in the marketplace

lines.text: Hear me, Beatrice,—
lines.plainText: Hear me Beatrice

lines.text: Talk with a man out at a window! a proper saying!
lines.plainText: Talk with a man out at a window a proper saying

lines.text: Nay, but Beatrice,—
lines.plainText: Nay but Beatrice

lines.text: Sweet Hero! she is wronged, she is slandered, she is undone.
lines.plainText: Sweet Hero she is wronged she is slandered she is undone

lines.text: Beat—
lines.plainText: Beat

lines.text: Princes and Counties! Surely, a princely testimony, a goodly Count Comfect; a sweet gallant, surely! O! that I were a man for his sake, or that I had any friend would be a man for my sake! But manhood is melted into curtsies, valour into compliment, and men are only turned into tongue, and trim ones too: he is now as valiant as Hercules, that only tells a lie and swears it. I cannot be a man with wishing, therefore I will die a woman with grieving.
lines.plainText: Princes and Counties Surely a princely testimony a goodly Count Comfect a sweet gallant surely O that I were a man for his sake or that I had any friend would be a man for my sake But manhood is melted into curtsies valour into compliment and men are only turned into tongue and trim ones too he is now as valiant as Hercules that only tells a lie and swears it I cannot be a man with wishing therefore I will die a woman with grieving

lines.text: Tarry, good Beatrice. By this hand, I love thee.
lines.plainText: Tarry good Beatrice By this hand I love thee

lines.text: Use it for my love some other way than swearing by it.
lines.plainText: Use it for my love some other way than swearing by it

lines.text: Think you in your soul the Count Claudio hath wronged Hero?
lines.plainText: Think you in your soul the Count Claudio hath wronged Hero

lines.text: Yea, as sure is I have a thought or a soul.
lines.plainText: Yea as sure is I have a thought or a soul

lines.text: Enough! I am engaged, I will challenge him. I will kiss your hand, and so leave you. By this hand, Claudio shall render me a dear account. As you hear of me, so think of me. Go, comfort your cousin: I must say she is dead; and so, farewell.
